examples.name: Basic
examples.description: A single checkbox with its visible label. The label is passed as the label prop, not as children: Checkbox renders label after the box, and children would reach the native input.

examples.name: Checked
examples.description: Uncontrolled and checked at first; the input keeps the value.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.description: The native disabled attribute: the checkbox can't be changed and leaves the tab order.

examples.name: Error message
examples.description: A single checkbox's own errorMessage: shown under the box, added to its aria-describedby, and marks it invalid, so invalid isn't needed with it.
examples.jsx: <Checkbox label="I've run a conflict check" required errorMessage="Run a conflict check before you open the matter." />

props.label: I've run a conflict check
props.errorMessage: Run a conflict check before you open the matter.

examples.name: Partial selection
examples.description: indeterminate on the checkbox that stands for a partly selected group, such as a select-all. It shows a dash and is announced as mixed; work out the next indeterminate from the items.

examples.name: No visible label
examples.description: A checkbox in a list row, named by aria-label because the row shows what it selects.

examples.name: Checkbox Group with an error
examples.description: A set of checkboxes under one legend, from options. Explain the error in words with errorMessage and set invalid with it.
examples.jsx:
<CheckboxGroup
  label="Send matter updates by"
  invalid
  errorMessage="Choose at least one way to send updates."
  options={[
    { value: 'email', label: 'Email' },
    { value: 'sms', label: 'SMS' },
  ]}
/>

props.label: Send matter updates by
props.errorMessage: Choose at least one way to send updates.

examples.name: Controlled Checkbox Group
examples.description: The checked values as an array in your state; onValueChange gets the next array, then the change event.

antiExamples.name: Checking the group's checkbox for a partial selection
antiExamples.reason: A checked select-all reads as all of its items being checked. When only some are, set indeterminate on it so it shows a dash and is announced as mixed.

antiExamples.name: No accessible name
antiExamples.reason: Without label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby the box still shows, but assistive technology can't say what it's for, and nothing warns you.

antiExamples.name: Invalid with no message
antiExamples.jsx: <CheckboxGroup label="Send matter updates by" invalid options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'sms', label: 'SMS' }]} />
antiExamples.reason: The red boxes alone don't say what's wrong, and not everyone can see the color. Pair invalid with an errorMessage that explains the problem.

antiExamples.name: One-option Checkbox Group to show an error
antiExamples.jsx: <CheckboxGroup label="Conflict check" invalid errorMessage="Run a conflict check." options={[{ value: 'done', label: "I've run a conflict check" }]} />
antiExamples.reason: The legend and the only option say the same thing twice. Give the single Checkbox its own errorMessage instead.

antiExamples.name: Wrapping a single Checkbox in Field for its error
antiExamples.jsx:
<Field label="Conflict check" state="error" message="Run a conflict check before you open the matter.">
  <Checkbox label="I've run a conflict check" />
</Field>
antiExamples.reason: Field's label replaces the checkbox's own label as its accessible name. Use the Checkbox's errorMessage for a single checkbox's error.

antiExamples.name: Checkboxes for mutually exclusive choices
antiExamples.jsx: <CheckboxGroup label="Preferred contact method" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />
antiExamples.reason: Checkboxes let people choose any number of options. When exactly one answer applies, use Radio Group, which keeps the choice to one.
